text: GALLAGHER: Next item is the update on Butterfield property proposal for shared services and discussion of village component at the site. I had set up a meeting last week with the county executive, legislator Tamanga and the town supervisor, Richard Shea to sorta…to figure out how we…where we were on the project…sorta…you know…see what we could do to help out. And it was a very productive meeting and everyone came out of that with some…some homework. And my job was to come to the Board and…to try to get an idea of what kind of services we could commit to up there. What would the village would wanna see up there. And a few of the ideas that had…some of them had been around already. And the idea is sorta get…for both the town and village to say what do you actually want. What do you have to contribute? And so… these are some of the ideas that came up. One of course is the post office…three thousand square foot to make this alternative location formally part of proposed project so when the post office puts out requests for lease offers this location can compete with any others. We would move forward on all options to have the best chance of having a best chance of having a location in cold spring for the post office. This location could very likely compete, price wise with any other location, which is one important factor that the post office will consider in making their decision. So…the best thing for us would be to have as many possibilities as possible. Hopefully one of those… because of that we will be able to keep the post office in cold spring. In thinking of uses for the village specifically, one thing that
prev: BEGINNING – 51m:45s AUDIO RECORDING – DISCUSSION OF BUTTERFIELD SITE
next: had been mentioned before and would probably makes sense is Cold Spring police station, it would be nice to keep here on Main Street but there is a problem, both due to space and due to the location of the post office upstairs. So in estimation is maybe fifteen hundred to two thousand square feet for that. There would be a cost to the village but it would make the police station compliant with the ADA… it would also free up space at village hall, which would either be used by the village or leased out. 3. Shared courtroom and justice court office…we’re thinking roughly two hundred and fifty square feet for the office. This would be shared with Philipstown. If the Philipstown project includes moving their court there then we could work with them on that. I did speak with Judge Costello…he’s not against the move…he does see the benefits for having a modern courtroom…but of course he’s also happy just where he is. This would have a cost to the village but would free up the current room for other village meetings and free up the judge’ office for village use, such as the building department office. 4. Is the Senior Center. That’s one that we’ve talked about for awhile now. And would certainly be the key…the most important part of this proposal. And 5. Is the firehouse that we’ve talked about for awhile… locating that on the site...What I wanted to do is get the board support for these options and see if there are any other ones for a discussion on these and see if there’s other ideas for the use of that. HUSTIS: There is one thing I was thinking actually as I was looking at the email….. Interrupted by Gallagher. GALLAGHER: Oh, I’m sorry I missed one…and that is sorta locating the trolley at the site in a secured garage space…so that would be one thing to add to that… so they don’t have to drive over from Carmel each time. HUSTIS: After reading this…I was thinking that…I was trying to make it out actually….If we come to an agreement that the firehouse go up on that section of the property and they leave the building where they are now on Main Street…Is that the one kind of idea for the police to be… and would that make it easier for the police to be there? GALLAGHER: Yeah.

text: When a Major Grading Application proposes earth movement involving 1,000CY or more or when a Remedial Grading Application proposes earth movement involving 5,000CY or more, the application shall be referred to the Planning Commission for a decision. Otherwise, all other Grading Applications shall be reviewed by the Community Development Director. The Director and/or the Planning Commission shall use the criteria contained in Section 17.76.040 of the City's Development Code in assessing an application for approval. If you have questions about these criteria, please contact the Planning staff.
